title: Palindrome Checker
description: Write a Java method that checks if a given string is a palindrome. A palindrome is a word, phrase, or sequence that reads the same forwards and backward. Your check should be case-insensitive and should ignore all non-alphanumeric characters (punctuation, spaces, etc.).
exampleInput:
Example 1: "Racecar"
Example 2: "hello"
Example 3: "A man, a plan, a canal: Panama"
exampleOutput:
Example 1: true
Example 2: false
Example 3: true

title: Recursive Fibonacci Sequence
description:
Write a recursive Java method to find the Nth number in the Fibonacci sequence. The Fibonacci sequence is a series of numbers where each number is the sum of the two preceding ones. The sequence starts with 0 and 1.

Base Cases: F(0) = 0, F(1) = 1.
Recursive Relation: F(N) = F(N-1) + F(N-2) for N > 1.

title: Rotate Array Left by K Positions
description: Write a Java method that rotates an array of integers to the left by a specified number of positions, `k`. In a left rotation, each element of the array is shifted one unit to the left, and the first element of the array becomes the last element.

title: Implement Insertion Sort
description: Write a Java method to sort an array of integers using the Insertion Sort algorithm. Insertion sort iterates through an input array and removes one element per iteration, finds the place the element belongs in the array, and then places it there.

title: Print a Mirrored Number Pattern
description: Given an integer N, write a Java program that prints a specific two-part, mirrored number and space pattern as shown in the example. Pay close attention to the number sequences and the spacing.

title: Singly Linked List Insertion
description:
Your task is to implement the insertion methods for a Singly Linked List from scratch. You will need to create a `Node` class and a `SinglyLinkedList` class. Implement the following two methods:

1.  `insertAtBeginning(int data)`: Adds a new node with the given data to the front of the list.
2.  `insertAtEnd(int data)`: Adds a new node with the given data to the end of the list.

title: Doubly Linked List Deletion
description:
Your task is to implement the deletion method for a Doubly Linked List from scratch. You will need a `Node` class (with `next` and `prev` pointers) and a `DoublyLinkedList` class. Implement the following method:

`deleteAtPosition(int position)`: Deletes the node at the given position (0-indexed). Handle edge cases like deleting the head, the tail, or a node from an empty/invalid list.
